title: Running time of a finite-state scanner
statement: Let $S$ be a finite set with decidable equality, let $\delta:S\times\{0,1\}\to S$ be a transition function, let $s_0\in S$ be a starting state, and let $A:S\to\{0,1\}$ be an acceptance predicate. The scanner built from these data computes, on every Boolean word $x$, the one-bit output $A(\operatorname{foldl}(\delta,s_0,x))$ in exactly $|x|+1$ steps.
replaced:
Let $S$ be a finite set with transition function
$\delta : S \times \{0,1\} \to S$, start state $s_0 \in S$, and accepting
predicate $\alpha$ on $S$. On every input $x$ of length $n$, the one-way scanner
built from these data halts within $n + 1$ steps, and its output is the
single bit $\alpha(\delta^*(s_0, x))$, where $\delta^*(s_0, x)$ is the state
reached by folding $\delta$ over $x$ from $s_0$.
